assumptions: The measured ligation frequencies (Potapov 2018) hold for the conditions the dataset was measured under.
limits: A dataset's temperature and buffer are its own; other conditions are not modelled.
Scores the junctions only, not the cutting of the parts.
bio.jane/contract.question: What fraction of assemblies will ligate every junction correctly with this overhang set, by measured T4 ligase data?

description: Score a Golden Gate junction (fusion-site) set against MEASURED T4 DNA ligase end-joining data. It is the number NEB's Ligase Fidelity Viewer reports: the expected fraction of assemblies in which EVERY junction ligated correctly. This is the quantitative counterpart to check_golden_gate_parts: that says whether the parts will be cut, this says whether the pieces will go back together in the right order. Wire golden_gate_assemble's `overhangs` output straight into it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

dataset.description: score against this measured matrix instead of the one the enzyme implies. Values: BsaI-HFv2 (BsaI-HFv2, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), BsmBI-v2 (BsmBI-v2, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), Esp3I (Esp3I, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), BbsI-HF (BbsI-HF, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), SapI (SapI, Golden Gate cycling (3 nt)), T4-01h-25C (T4 DNA ligase, 1 h at 25 C (4 nt)), T4-01h-37C (T4 DNA ligase, 1 h at 37 C (4 nt)), T4-18h-25C (T4 DNA ligase, 18 h at 25 C (4 nt)), T4-18h-37C (T4 DNA ligase, 18 h at 37 C (4 nt)).

enzyme.description: the Type-IIS enzyme the reaction uses, which picks that enzyme's own measured matrix when one exists. Only applies when dataset is not given.

overhangs.description: the junction overhangs, one per junction, top strand (e.g. AATG, GCTT). Wire `golden_gate_assemble.overhangs` here, or list them.

remedies.description: also compute what to CHANGE: the drop-the-worst repair, and replacement candidates for each flagged junction. Off makes the run cheaper on a large set.

replacements_per_junction.description: how many replacement candidates to rank per flagged junction. Advanced.

name: score_overhang_fidelity

atMeasurementCeiling.description: true when NO mismatch ligation was measured between any two junctions, so the score is exactly 100%: the floor the source experiment can resolve, not a guarantee

dataset.description: the measured matrix actually scored against

flags.description: weak, self-misannealing and cross-misannealing junction indices, plus the structural verdict

junctions.description: per junction: overhang, correct/total measured events, its own fidelity, Watson-Crick strength, and its strongest mismatch partners

meaningful.description: false when a STRUCTURAL error makes the fidelity number misleading rather than merely bad: do not present `fidelity` on its own when this is false

percent.description: the same number as a percentage, which is how every incumbent reports it

repair.description: the drop-the-worst repair: which junctions to remove, what is left, and the fidelity that leaves. Null when `remedies` is off

replacements.description: per FLAGGED junction, the best overhangs to swap in, each with the whole set’s fidelity after the swap. Empty when `remedies` is off

worst.description: the weakest junctions, worst first: what to change to raise the score
